name: Transaction Boundary Conformance
rule: Transaction boundaries were not moved for aesthetic reasons. Where a boundary is implicit or missing, it is recorded as debt with the reason it was not changed in a refactoring phase.

operations.lock_ordering: Screen rows locked first, in deterministic id order, before any availability or capacity read
operations.event_timing: BookingCreated dispatched at the END of the transaction, not after commit (pre-existing)
operations.queued_side_effects: none - notification goes through the event subscriber synchronously
operations.notes: Extracted from BookingController in Phase 0.13 with the boundary unchanged. All four business rejections occur before the first write, so raising an exception instead of returning an HTTP response rolls back an empty transaction - observably identical to the previous early return.

operations.locking: lockForUpdate on the merged existing+target screen set
operations.lock_ordering: Union of old and new screens, deduplicated, then locked
operations.notes: Extracted in Phase 0.13, boundary unchanged. Note the pre-existing gap: reschedule can change end_time/quantities/screen_id without recomputing pricing or re-running revenue distribution.

Still inline in the controller and not consolidated with CreateCampaignBookingUseCase: the legacy channel trusts the client-supplied price and writes no pricing snapshot, so unifying it would change financial behaviour.

operations.transaction_boundary: no DB transaction around the gateway call
operations.notes: Architecture Rule 4 satisfied: the external network call is not held inside a row lock.

operations.transaction_boundary: gateway call isolated from DB locks
operations.notes: Phase 0.9. Rule 4: external network operation is not performed while holding row locks.

operations.notes: approveMedia, rejectMedia, startSession, endSession, extendSession, markMediaReview, markManualPayment are all multi-write without a transaction. Pre-existing.
